subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: The atom pair
hotspots.description: A neutral sodium atom and a neutral chlorine atom, about to trade an electron and become ions.
hotspots.positionHint: The two atoms with their shell rings.
hotspots.function: Shows the atoms that will become ions.

hotspots.label: Sodium loses → Na⁺
hotspots.description: Sodium gives away its one outer electron. Now it has more protons than electrons — so it becomes positive Na⁺.
hotspots.positionHint: The sodium atom, losing its electron in the transfer layer.
hotspots.function: Shows losing electrons creating a positive ion.

hotspots.label: Chlorine gains → Cl⁻
hotspots.description: Chlorine accepts the electron. Now it has more electrons than protons — so it becomes negative Cl⁻.
hotspots.positionHint: The chlorine atom, gaining the electron in the transfer layer.
hotspots.function: Shows gaining electrons creating a negative ion.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A sodium atom and a chlorine atom float side by side, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Sodium: soft muted violet with one outer electron; chlorine: soft muted green with seven; shell rings translucent hairline. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots and the transfer electron (amber / coral / molecular-green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Sodium sphere: soft muted violet matte, roughness ~0.5. Chlorine sphere: soft muted green matte, roughness ~0.5. Shell rings: translucent hairline, alpha ~0.25. Electron dots: small teal, roughness ~0.4. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a sodium and chlorine atom becoming ions, built to be read as 'lose an electron → positive; gain an electron → negative.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: two atoms side by side (spacing ~1.7): LEFT sodium (soft muted violet sphere radius ~0.55) with a shell ring carrying ONE teal electron; RIGHT chlorine (soft muted green sphere radius ~0.5) with a shell ring carrying SEVEN teal electrons, one spot clearly empty. Both neutral.

2) TRANSFER (toggleable layer): a curved dashed path arcs from sodium's lone electron to chlorine's empty spot; the electron dot animates along it (app-driven) and arrives in chlorine's empty slot.

3) CHARGE AND ATTRACTION (toggleable layer): a soft + glyph appears over sodium and a − glyph over chlorine (app-drawn UI glyphs, not mesh text), and the two atoms ease closer together with a soft glow band between them — the ions attracting.

Camera: framed so both atoms fit with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 7-11k triangles. Named nodes: SodiumAtom, ChlorineAtom, ShellRing_Na, ShellRing_Cl, SodiumElectron_01, ChlorineElectrons_07, TransferPath, TransferDot, AttractionBand. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
